title: Data sovereignty & retention: automated audit playbook and tenant isolation attestations for Dedicated
creator: Anika Shah
description: Implement an automated end-to-end audit playbook that generates signed tenant isolation attestations and retention evidence packages for Dedicated capacity customers. The playbook will collect residency metadata (region tags, storage locations, backup locations), retention policy snapshots, system configuration (VPC/subnet, KMS key ARNs), and runtime isolation proofs (network ACLs, process namespace mappings, pod/node affinity). Output artifacts must be tamper-evident, human-readable summaries, and machine-readable bundles suitable for customer delivery and internal SOC review.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook can be triggered manually and on a schedule (cron) for a given tenant in Dedicated and produces a single archive (.zip) containing: residency_manifest.json, retention_snapshot.csv, signed_attestation.pdf, and system_config.yaml
Signed attestation uses org-wide signing key and includes timestamp, tenant id, region, and assertion statements about data residency and retention settings
Evidence bundle includes verifiable S3 locations (or on-prem storage pointers) and checksums; minimal PII redaction applied per legal guidance
Automation produces a dataset of audit metrics (token-level logs omitted) ingestible by Console for tenant audit history UI
End-to-end test covering happy path and failure modes (missing KMS key, cross-region snapshot) present in CI and green
Playbook adheres to security_review_required gating and gets sign-off from Legal and Security before release
Documentation (Runbook + customer-facing attestation FAQ) published to Drive and linked in Console
implementation_notes: Spike (2026-02-15): explored approaches: agent-based collector vs agentless APIs. Chose hybrid: agentless metadata via control plane + short-lived collector job for runtime evidence where necessary to avoid long-lived agents on customer nodes.

Collector runs as a privileged one-shot job in tenant's dedicated cluster with bounded lifetime and RBAC-minimized service account. Collector writes to customer-residency-bucket under tenant-scoped prefix with server-side-encryption and KMS key alias=redwood/dedicated/attest

Residency_manifest schema: {tenant_id, primary_region, permitted_regions, storage_backends:[{type, location_uri, kms_alias}], backups:[{frequency, last_snapshot_ts}]}. We'll version schema as v1.0 and include schema.json in bundle
Retention_snapshot exported from Config DB and applied retention_config_hash; include human-readable policy and machine hash used for regression detection
Signed attestation generated by signing service (infra/signing-service) using HSM-managed key; service API: POST /sign/attestation returns PDF and JWS envelope. Use audit log correlation id.
Evidence bundles will be uploaded to an internal S3 audit-bucket for SOC review and pushed to customer S3 endpoint (if configured) or emailed link via secure presigned URL for 7-day window
Telemetry: emit events to metrics pipeline (audit.playbook.run.start, .success, .failure) with tags: tenant_id, region, collector_version
Backward compatibility: for older dedicated tenants lacking control-plane hooks, fallback to manual checklist generation and include manual_confirmation.txt with required steps
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary) - 2026-03-20: run playbook against two internal test tenants and one pilot customer tenant; collect results and iterate on attestation language
Phase 2 (restricted) - 2026-03-27: enable self-serve generation for customers on Dedicated with opt-in flag; surface evidence links in Console under Security > Audit Reports
Phase 3 (general) - 2026-04-01: open to all Dedicated customers and add scheduled monthly audit runs with retention of 12 months in internal audit-bucket
Communication: announce to pilot customers, CSB, and account reps; include sample attestation and FAQ
Rollback criteria: >2 pilot failures OR evidence of leaked temporary presigned URLs OR legal/security objection to attestation wording
qa_checks: Unit tests for manifest serialization and schema validation
Integration test: collector job runs in ephemeral cluster, writes bundle to staging audit-bucket, signing-service returns JWS envelope
E2E: end-to-end generation to a staging customer and retrieval of bundle via presigned URL
Security tests: RBAC audit for collector service account, KMS key policy validation, pentest checklist item completed
Performance: full playbook run for medium tenant completes within 8 minutes; build CI test asserting <10m runtime
